LESSON: CHEMICAL BONDING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.3: Chemical bonding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Chemical bonding, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How do bond types relate to physical properties of compounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers the role of valence electrons in bond formation. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by peers, learner support assistant or teacher as they give their views,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers the role of valence electrons in bond formation. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by peers, learner support assistant or teacher as they give their views,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Chemical bonding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such

as utensils and other cookware.

● Digital literacy: the learner navigates through online sources to access virtual laboratories for simulations on formation

of chemical bonds.

● Creativity and imagination: as the learner undertakes a project of modelling ball and stick ionic and covalent structures

of selected molecules using locally available resources.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner recognises and appreciates the input of every group member when discussing the relationship

between bond types and physical properties of different structures.

● Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other

cookware.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and Security: as the learner observes safety precautions when carrying out activities to investigate properties of

elements and compounds.

● Financial Literacy: as the learner makes informed decisions when selecting appropriate items, appliances and equipment

made from specific elements and compounds.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Textbooks, Periodic table chart, Equipped chemistry laboratory, First Aid kit, Online resources, educational videos,

interactive simulations, adapted digital devices, locally available materials (such as Cardboard or manilla paper, wires or

strings, plasticine, beads or bottle tops), Adapted writing resources,
